​ @LEK but at what framerate though? Higher framerate makes the FG look better and minimal input latency, but if you're getting really high fps native then FG is pointless.

Alternatively, FG at low fps (10 for example) will lower your native fps to 9 and then double it to be 18 but can still only interact with native frames, so input delay becomes awful.

Best case is somewhere in between in order to reach your monitors refresh rate, but not if you're getting below 60 fps to begin with.

text:
⁠​⁠ @brunocerny  frame gen is just advanced frame interpolation, it looks at two real frames and figures out what it would look like between the 2. Lower fps means farther distance between the frames meaning it’s trying to cover a longer distance in the same amount of frames. Higher fps means shorter distance and filling in the blanks is a lot more accurate. By principal FG requires a high fps to look good.

Edit: generated frames also don’t take into account inputs, causing a delay. Your character doesn’t move in a different direction until the next real frame when it calculates your input, nor does it shoot if you were to click. That leads to you not being able to dodge an attack, make a difficult platforming jump, or attack an enemy for example. If you don’t hold click long enough to be picked up by the next real frame, you simply wont shoot/attack.
